nodes.label: Classifier State Machine (Committed / Deferral / OverrideStream)
nodes.rationale: Deferral and OverrideStream classifiers wrap a CommittedClassifier as base so shared behavior lives in one place.

nodes.label: Trace-Log Replay (tracing-tree)
nodes.rationale: Works purely from the hierarchical tracing logs the core already emits, so no changes to the classifier are needed.

nodes.label: Inference vs Classification
nodes.rationale: Inference is the cheap sequential model weighing constraints; classification is the expensive ground truth kept off the inference thread.

nodes.label: Context Layer (structural state)
nodes.rationale: Holds current_parent, decided pages, prev_parents and guarantee_failures; it informs inference but never decides.

nodes.label: Four-Tier Constraint Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Ordered Definitive -> Hard -> Soft -> Overrides. Tiers must not be mixed: no scoring in hard constraints, no filtering in soft ones.

nodes.label: Inference Layer (cheap, speculative, main-thread)
nodes.rationale: Fast, reversible and allowed to be wrong; kept separate from classification so expensive work never blocks guessing.

nodes.label: Tier 3 Soft Constraints
nodes.rationale: Score budget is intentionally kept around 1.2-1.5 to leave room for future constraints.

nodes.label: Constraints Instead of Static Weights
nodes.rationale: Rather than static REWARD_* weight constants, behaviour is expressed as hard (structural) and soft (rewarding) constraint types; this abstracts checking out of the classifier, eases tracing, and is statically dispatched for efficiency.

nodes.label: z Score Budget (softcap +/-3.0)
nodes.rationale: All soft contributions are soft-capped at |z| <= 3.0: +/-1.5 for structural constraints, +/-1.0 for dynamic weights, +/-0.5 buffer.

nodes.label: Constraint-Based Speculative Sequence Labeling
nodes.rationale: The engine is parsing / constraint satisfaction / sequence labeling, not ML: no model, no training, no learned weights. 'Inference' means constraint-driven deduction and scoring is a fixed linear tally; any change that looks like learned weights should stop.

nodes.label: Speculative Guess, Selective Classify Validation
nodes.rationale: Ground-truth classify() calls user C++ that pokes MuPDF and is expensive, so the engine guesses each page's type cheaply on the main thread from context + constraints and only fires classify() for the single top guess, in parallel off-thread.

nodes.label: Static Constraint Dispatch (impl_constraint_enum!)
nodes.rationale: Proc macro generates a matching enum with direct dispatch: no vtables, no allocation, full inlining.

nodes.label: ContextUpdates (incremental revert)
nodes.rationale: Replaying updates backward is still slow and discards inferred state from the rest of the batch, making re-inference more expensive.

nodes.label: Python-Orchestrated Build Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Ordering matters: Rust generated/ files and C++ headers must exist before cargo build; build.rs locates MuPDF and headers via CLASSIFIER_BUILD_DIR and links the user's classifier_intermediary.

nodes.label: Independent vs Dependent Objects
nodes.rationale: Independent (organizational) objects are safe anchors meaningful without prior context and terminate deferral/override-stream regions; dependent objects are only meaningful relative to a parent and unsafe to infer once context is poisoned.

nodes.label: Known Incomplete Areas
nodes.rationale: Deferral anchor scan can walk past a real anchor and pair parity is seeded without checking the last decision; OverrideAction::ClassifyAs is unused; Context has no rollback.

nodes.label: Tier 4 Overrides (Override / OverrideStream)
nodes.rationale: OverrideStream bypasses hierarchy inference across a recognized structural run so the engine avoids entering deferral for a known-shaped region.

nodes.label: PDF Classifier v5 AI Agent Instructions
nodes.norm_label: pdf classifier v5 ai agent instructions

nodes.label: Context Snapshot/Rollback Problems
nodes.rationale: Reverting context n pages back would need n clones per batch (size), excessive allocations on large documents, and risky management of n states passed among workers.

nodes.label: Deferral Recovery (Forward Anchoring)
nodes.rationale: A wrong guess poisons running structural context; instead of snapshot-and-rollback the engine scans forward to the next independent anchor and backfills the gap structurally, giving linear-time recovery with no exponential backtracking and no per-page context snapshots.

nodes.label: MuPDF Thread-Affine Contexts
nodes.rationale: MuPDF fz_context cannot cross threads, so every WorkerThread owns an isolated context + document.

nodes.label: Opaque FFI Boundary (cxx bridge)
nodes.rationale: Raw MuPDF types are never exposed across Rust<->C++; everything is an opaque wrapper (OpaqueCtx, OpaqueDoc, SharedData, OpaqueResult) with UniquePtr cleanup.

nodes.label: Structural Knowledge as O(1) Lookup Tables
nodes.norm_label: structural knowledge as o(1) lookup tables
nodes.rationale: Schema relationships (VALID_CHILDREN, VALID_PARENTS, VALID_PAIRS, INDEPENDENTS) are compiled to adjacency matrices at build time to replace recursive tree walks with constant-time lookups.

nodes.label: Three-Language Split (Python / C++ / Rust)
nodes.rationale: Each language exists because of an orthogonal hard constraint: Python for schema reflection and the DSL, C++ for MuPDF's C ABI and thread-affine contexts, Rust for safe parallel scheduling and the state machine. Collapsing any two layers violates one of those constraints.

nodes.label: Worker-Affine Extraction
nodes.rationale: The classify Shared payload holds MuPDF objects tied to the classifying worker's fz_context, so the auto-queued extract job must return to that same worker (re-queued if busy).

nodes.label: Pre-allocating Known-Size Vecs
nodes.rationale: Pre-size collections whose length is known (classified_results ~ total_pages) but not tiny ones like the ~20-byte constraint vecs.

nodes.label: classifier_intermediary (colordoc)
nodes.rationale: Target name is fixed because pdf_classifier_core/build.rs links classifier_intermediary out of ${CLASSIFIER_BUILD_DIR}/lib.

nodes.label: colordoc Diagnostic Harness
nodes.rationale: colordoc's classification/extraction logic is guaranteed correct, so any wrong result isolates a bug in the classifier engine itself.

nodes.label: Per-Page Ground Truth Generation
nodes.rationale: The static-classifier export supplies the authoritative chapter/subchapter sequence but lacks page numbers, so PDF text signatures position every page; anchors are sequence-aligned to the export and generation aborts if any anchor cannot be positioned.

nodes.label: Datatable Visualization (Python)
nodes.rationale: Moved from a C++ DataTable extension to Python to avoid polluting the datatable namespace; needed only for debugging.

nodes.label: Original Static Classifier
nodes.rationale: A previous, hard-to-understand classifier for the example document type; its techniques were reimplemented here and its per-object tests were regenerated with AI.

nodes.label: AI as C++ Teacher and Concept Tester
nodes.norm_label: ai as c++ teacher and concept tester
nodes.rationale: Rust-proven ideas may not account for C++ memory unsafety, so AI is used to test existing concepts and teach unfamiliar syntax (constrained templates, [[nodiscard]]), not to conceive solutions.

nodes.label: AI Usage Criteria
nodes.rationale: AI is allowed only for tasks that are time-consuming with little development value (boilerplate), are not intellectually showcase-worthy, would cause burnout through repetition, or merely reintegrate the author's own existing solution.

nodes.label: Breaking vs Non-Breaking Objects
nodes.rationale: A safer model guesses the non-breaking option (e.g. diagram over subchapter) because a wrong breaking guess invalidates downstream inference.

nodes.label: Deferred Block
nodes.rationale: When a breaking object fails classification, subsequent dependent pages are poisoned; store them as a deferred block until the next independent object, then re-infer the block relative to the actual result.

nodes.label: Anchored Classification for Shallow Hierarchies
nodes.rationale: For shallow hierarchies, classify every page only against independents (chapter/subchapter) and infer diagram-table pairs between anchors; c = i*o classify calls and dependent pages only need extract, avoiding constant deferral.

nodes.label: panic! in the Classifier Hot Path
nodes.norm_label: panic! in the classifier hot path
nodes.rationale: Inference must stay fast: with n threads, inference time i and classify time c, n*i < c must hold so a batch of inferences finishes before classification in case the engine must yield for a defer.

nodes.label: Page Cursor Discipline (PageLock)
nodes.rationale: Page advancement is enforced by a type because historically the worst bugs came from advancing the cursor in the wrong place (double-advances, skips).
